I will still do it the way people around me do, but I will not farm too lightly. I only have 7.7 mu, so every bag I buy matters, and with some family members working outside, I also need the work to be manageable. I have only farmed 2 years, so I will start from what worked last year in this area and adjust a little. Around Quzhou, if wheat gets too little fertilizer, the heads stay small, and if maize gets too little after wheat, the ears are short. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. I do have well water, so I will use irrigation to hold the crop steady. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put enough base fertilizer, water a few times at key stages, and spray 2 times if disease or aphids show. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what many people use now and the yield is steadier, give it a solid fertilizer dose, water in the important periods, and spray 2 times for weeds and insects if needed. I will use rotary tillage because it is simpler for my size and fits the wheat-maize rotation better than heavy ploughing every season.
